chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Chuckles stays with his wife and Green feels letdown
summary: Chuckles wants two more years with his wife, Green says the delay is a letdown and worries about the public forgetting them.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: because we grew up together, you see. All right, he had me, so what could I do. I had to bend over backwards, and that's what I did. So, like I'm saying, she was such a wonderful girl -- she still is. I think she's in Illinois or somewhere out there. She made Chuckles very happy. I'd never seen him that happy since we were children, you see. But, like I say, I went and explained to him that I wasn't going to be mingling with the public out in, you know, amongst people and they'd be questioning me and what are we doing and why aren't you, and so on, you know, and why don't you do this and why -- are you going to, see. Rather than to go through all of this I said I think I would go back to a hospital, you see, and let them re-examine me and I would get permission to go in there, but I'd have to get a voucher. So, now --
I'm not sure I understand, Chuck. How were you feeling now that Chuckles had left? Did -- you both had an agreement, or what?

An agreement that he wanted to stay with his wife, you know. He wants to be, you know, you know -- for two years. At least one anniversary, see -- that's what that entails. I mean, if they was married one year, so that's the beginning, that's the first anniversary.
And then what would happen after the

We were supposed to reunion as Chuck and Chuckles, but we'd still be stars. Well, he says he would like two more years, you see. (Laughter). What happens to the stardom? Out of sight, out of mind, you see.
So, what, what -- you were feeling, I imagine, very depressed.

Yes, it was a letdown for me because I didn't like to neglect the public, you see. I love people -- they grow on you. Especially when you're traveling and you meet so many different, you know, people. Degrees of the population, and it kind of grows on you. You kind of get like you want to be a father, a brother -- you just want to be more to the people than you already are, see.
So, Chuckles wouldn't go back with you?

Well, he did not go. He preferred to do these two -- he was going to go, but, I mean, we could put it off two more years and we were friendly enough -- we were friends enough to do that, you know. I'd say, 'Yeah, we're friends, but what about the people out there? What about them? They're going to want to know what became of us, what happened to us?'
